statement: A capture-first note surface renders one column of entries separated by dividers — no cards, no list-pane/editor-pane split, no destination choice before typing.
mechanismHypothesis: Every visual boundary (card edge, pane border) and every pre-capture decision (which pane, which type) is a unit of friction paid before or during writing. A single stream with dividers spends the entire friction budget on zero-to-first-keystroke, which is the job of a capture tool. The three-pane pattern spends it on retrieval structure instead — a different job.
appliesWhen: the surface's primary job is capture or review-in-time-order
organization is emergent (tags, links) rather than upfront (folders first)
doesNotApplyWhen: long-form documents with internal heading hierarchy (obs-fabric-contrast/f1)
workflows where retrieval at 10k+ items dominates capture (obs-evernote-contrast/f1)
multi-user triage queues where list-vs-detail is load-bearing
confidenceBasis: Derived from one source-grounded positive (owner-owned Mew checkout, file:line locators) plus Mobbin counterexamples; no audience-task evidence yet, so confidence is capped below audience-proven per the M-tier rule.
reVerifyReason: Mew is under active development in the owner-local checkouts and Mobbin comparators drift with product releases; re-inspect the live surfaces and re-read global.css before continuing to cite these facts.
tierLadder: M2: live shipped-product observation (owner-owned source checkout with file:line locators, plus Mobbin live screens). M1 documentation not consulted. M3 audience-task evidence absent — no rule here may be promoted to audience-proven until a real capture task is observed.

boundToGate.reason: Governs entry-list rendering node-platform does not implement; the assertion belongs to the consuming note surface, not to the platform that derived the rule.
